task.name: A body whose sections contradict its declared type passes the shape gate, so a bug re-typed as a feature spec enters a sprint unchallenged
task.story_text:
## Why

The shape gate treats every rejection reason at one severity, and its heuristics have no rule for a body whose sections contradict its declared type. Two bugs in the last two weeks (#2335, #2445) carried full `## Acceptance criteria` sections — the shape the authoring guide reserves for feature-type issues and explicitly prohibits on bugs — and both passed intake. Both went on to above-median sprint cost (#2335: three runs, seven review cycles). Meanwhile the defects that are only *suspicions* — test-requirement phrasing, fix-location prescription in a diagnosed bug's notes — measurably do not predict bad outcomes in the same window, so blocking on them would trade real work for false positives.

The gate needs two tiers: a structural contradiction between the declared type and the body's sections is a refusal; a phrase-level suspicion is advisory.

## Acceptance criteria

- A body whose sections contradict its declared type is refused at intake, with a reason naming the contradicting section and the type rule it violates. The contradiction set is derived from the authoring guide's per-type reserved-section rules, not from a list private to this issue; a section the guide does not reserve for any type is never a contradiction on its own.
- Phrase-level suspicions surface as advisory notices attached to the verdict without changing it, and an issue carrying only advisory notices remains runnable.
- A body that triggers neither tier produces the same verdict it does today — the new rules introduce no refusal class for bodies the guide's type shapes permit.
- The verdict output distinguishes the two tiers so a caller (or operator) can tell a refusal from advice without parsing prose.

## Example

Today, this body with the `bug` label passes the gate:

```
## Observed
Contract tests never run in CI.
## Expected
Provider argv drift is caught before release.
## Acceptance criteria
- A `make test-contract` target exists that sets THEFORGE_RUN_CLI_CONTRACT=1
```

After this change it is refused with a reason of the form: `bug body carries an acceptance-criteria section; bugs use observed/expected (see authoring guide)`. The same body with the acceptance-criteria section removed and a Notes line reading "the fix belongs in `runners/api.py`" passes, with an advisory notice on the verdict noting the fix-location phrasing.

## Notes

Origin: authoring-quality audit of issues #2136–#2501 (2026-08-17). The two structural offenders were the only defect class in the window that both escaped the gate and correlated with elevated cost; phrase-level defects (28 issues flagged) ran *cheaper* than the clean cohort because they concentrate in forge-diagnosed bugs, the best-performing cohort. Hence block/warn rather than block/block.

reviews.summary: [openai-gpt-5.5-cli] The type-shape refusal works, but the new advisory plumbing can label a refused diagnosis verdict as non-blocking advice. | [anthropic-opus-cli] Two-tier shape gate works and the new refusal/advisory verdicts are correct, but a refused issue is now also published in the non-blocking advisory tier with the identical reason code, so the blocking/advisory distinction the spec asks for is not actually observable.

findings.description: When an investigation-ready bug has an unknown confirmed cause, the sprint shape gate records the issue in both skipped and advisories, so the advisory warning says the issue is not blocking while the same issue is refused from the sprint.

An issue that the gate refuses is also published as a non-blocking advisory carrying the same reason code, so a bug whose Diagnosis asserts no confirmed cause is reported both as blocked with verdict diagnosis_cause_unknown and in the advisory banner as carrying diagnosis_cause_unknown "not blocking", and two skip events are written for the same issue and code, one blocking and one advisory.
A new typed verdict identifier is emitted by the shape gate and written to the audit substrate while the ADR that declares the verdict surface bounded to an explicit list still omits it.

The acceptance-criteria heading spelling set is written out a third time as a new module-private constant, duplicating the identical literal already inlined in the parsing helper and in the intake renderer.

The test-requirement advisory fires on descriptive diagnosis prose rather than prescriptive phrasing, so a Diagnosis Evidence bullet reading "the failing run needs the contract tests enabled before release" is annotated as prescribing tests.

plan_review.findings:
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 4 assumes ADVISORY reasons can be threaded to ShapeGateResult.advisories, but the admissible path in classify_admissibility (admissibility.py:262-270) returns reason_codes=() and detail='' — advisory reasons are only reachable via the Admissibility.result ShapeResult, and SkippedIssue requires title/detail/verdict fields (today only reopened_stale_contract populates them, shape_gate.py:446).
  Suggestion: Have shape_gate build advisory SkippedIssue entries from adm.result.reasons filtered on Severity.ADVISORY (verdict='' as the reopen advisory already does), or add an explicit advisory_codes/advisory_detail field to Admissibility rather than relying on reason_codes.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 2's instruction to 'insert the check before existing exemptions such as check_missing_acceptance_criteria can silently bypass bug-format bodies' misreads the pipeline: check.py:56-71 runs each check independently and collects all reasons, so the is_bug_format_issue exemption is internal to check_missing_acceptance_criteria and no ordering change is needed or sufficient.
  Suggestion: Drop the ordering framing; add the new contradiction check as an independent entry in the check.py tuple and rely on derive_verdict precedence for which verdict wins.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] The new refusal class has no remediation path: intake groom's AC-scaffolding stubs (groom_flow.py _restructure_feature_body, shape_render.py _restructure_enhancement) only add AC sections for feature-classified bodies, so a refused bug body offers the operator no mechanical fix and no groom finding code.
  Suggestion: Optionally emit a groom finding (or at minimum ensure the refusal detail states the removal action) so the operator sees the recovery step; not required by any AC.

finding_registry.description: When an investigation-ready bug has an unknown confirmed cause, the sprint shape gate records the issue in both skipped and advisories, so the advisory warning says the issue is not blocking while the same issue is refused from the sprint.

An issue that the gate refuses is also published as a non-blocking advisory carrying the same reason code, so a bug whose Diagnosis asserts no confirmed cause is reported both as blocked with verdict diagnosis_cause_unknown and in the advisory banner as carrying diagnosis_cause_unknown "not blocking", and two skip events are written for the same issue and code, one blocking and one advisory.
A new typed verdict identifier is emitted by the shape gate and written to the audit substrate while the ADR that declares the verdict surface bounded to an explicit list still omits it.

The acceptance-criteria heading spelling set is written out a third time as a new module-private constant, duplicating the identical literal already inlined in the parsing helper and in the intake renderer.

The test-requirement advisory fires on descriptive diagnosis prose rather than prescriptive phrasing, so a Diagnosis Evidence bullet reading "the failing run needs the contract tests enabled before release" is annotated as prescribing tests.

When an investigation-ready bug also contains fix-location phrasing, sprint intake refuses it for diagnosis_cause_unknown but puts bug_fix_location_prescription in the skipped reason codes, so the phrase-level advisory is emitted downstream as a blocking skip reason.

The type-shape rule record declares a contradicted-section slug that is populated for all four issue types but read by no code path, so the refusal message names the offending section from the parsed heading text while the declared slug never reaches any output.

The module declares a second diagnosis-heading pattern constant holding the same expression as the existing public one 125 lines further down, so two names in one module describe the same heading vocabulary.

An enhancement-labelled body written in the bug-report section shape is refused with the typed verdict needs_diagnosis and the operator description "bug filing has no diagnosis section; run forge diagnose to investigate", so the machine-readable routing signal points at a bug-only producer while the type-shape contradiction that actually explains the refusal appears only at the tail of a long prose detail.

When an issue is refused with several blocking reason codes and the selected verdict comes from a later code in the list, the intake remediation outcome event records the first reason code as the issue's shape_verdict, so an enhancement written in bug-report shape is stored with shape_verdict needs_diagnosis while the shape gate's own verdict event for the same issue records needs_grooming_type_shape.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules

Keep modules single-purpose. Extract when a responsibility separates from its neighbours — never to satisfy a line count. Putting a change in an already-large module is correct if that is where it belongs; a module carved at whatever line got the count down is worse than the large module it came from.
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.
